name: Iowa

notes: Food for home is exempt from the state and local taxes, but candy, soft drinks and dietary supplements are taxed at 6% plus the local tax, which is not counted here.
Alcohol is taxed at 6% plus the local tax, on top of excise taxes left out here: beer $5.89 a barrel, wine $1.75 a gallon, and the state markup on liquor (up to 50% of the wholesale price).

Cigarettes and other tobacco are taxed at 6% plus the local tax, on top of excise taxes left out here: $1.36 a pack of cigarettes, 50% of the wholesale price on most other tobacco (cigars at most 50 cents each), snuff $1.19 an ounce.
Household supplies: diapers are exempt, which is not taken out here.
Personal care products: menstrual products are exempt, which is not taken out here.
Barber and beauty services are taxed.
Clothing is taxed, except clothing and footwear under $100 on the first Friday and Saturday of August (August 7 and 8, 2026).
Laundry and dry cleaning are taxed; self-service washers and dryers aren't.
Motor fuel is exempt from the sales tax and pays a per-gallon tax instead (gasoline 30 cents; E-15 and higher blends 28 cents from July 1, 2026; diesel 32.5 cents), left out here.
Auto repair labor: vehicle repair is taxed.

Hotel stays pay a 5% state hotel and motel tax instead of the sales tax (the local option tax doesn't apply) plus a local hotel tax of up to 7% where a city or county levies one (most that do levy 7%, for 12% in all, as in Des Moines, Cedar Rapids and Davenport); not counted here.
The services below are from the Department of Revenue's list of taxable services.
gaps: Iowa's 1% local option tax is adopted by each city and by each county for its unincorporated area; the rates here are from the Department of Revenue's list effective July 1, 2026, by city and county part.

Ankeny's 1% local option tax, approved by its voters on September 8, 2026, starts January 1, 2027 (City of Ankeny) and isn't in the rates here. Greene, Poweshiek and Ringgold counties' taxes are set to end June 30, 2027 (Grinnell has renewed its own) and Wayne County's December 31, 2027 (the Department's list). On September 8, 2026 Wayne County's unincorporated area and its towns voted on a new 1% tax from January 1, 2028: it passed everywhere but Clio and Millerton, whose votes were tied (unofficial results, Wayne County Auditor).
Yessdale, on the Department's list, isn't a 2024 Census place; its tracts take its county's rate.
Saylorville, on the Department's list, is an unincorporated Census place rather than a city; it takes Polk County's rate for unincorporated areas (no local option tax), as the list gives it.

programs: Tax increment areas are mapped for Des Moines, Dubuque, Waterloo and Linn County's cities (Cedar Rapids, Marion, Hiawatha and others); other cities' urban renewal areas are listed in the Department of Management's Urban Renewal Report System but have no maps here. A 2026 law (SF 2472) ends urban renewal ordinances adopted after May 18, 2026 after 23 years and gives existing ones without an end date 20 more years, after which they keep at most 60% of the increment. Self-supported municipal improvement districts are mapped for Cedar Rapids only. Main Street districts are those of Main Street Iowa's September 2026 list of 53 communities; Fairfield's and Indianola's have no mapped boundary. Iowa's enterprise zones ended in 2014.

warn.text: Altoona draws many visitors (the Prairie Meadows casino and racetrack and Adventureland), but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy: its seasonal homes (0.4%) and its 17 lodging places (0.8 per 1,000 residents) fall under the flag's cutoffs over the city as a whole, though the census tract that holds 13 of them (2.9 per 1,000 residents) is flagged on its own. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.
